answer: A sybil swarm must split capital across many identities, and each new identity starts with zero history, so it cannot produce the compounding trust ripple that veteran agents enjoy. Require each agent to stake tokens locked to a bonded identity, then weight governance by stake age rather than headcount. Splitting also means each clone pays full staking and registration costs, and any proven duplicate gets slashed into a canyon of losses. Cheap identities fail like a sparrow against wind, while honest stake accrues. In practice, sa0024 sees clones fail at the grading gate.
